draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kazhakoottam! With Technopark close by, it's called the IT capital of Kerala. But it was once the power base of Ugran Pillai, who rebelled against King Marthanda Varma.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat here, so ask a local where the Technopark crowd goes.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Sri Ganapathi Temple is a minute away, Attinkuzhy Devi Temple is about 13 min, and a Krishna Temple is around 14 min on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head toward Pallithura, where the name means 'the beach beside the church'.
moodReplies.surprise-me: In 1962 the villagers of nearby Pallithura gave up most of their village for the Thumba rocket launching station, which led to ISRO.

spots.name: Sri Ganapathi Temple
spots.detail: 1 min walk · Right next to you

spots.name: Attinkuzhy Devi Temple
spots.detail: 13 min walk · A local Devi temple

legends.title: A thousand-year-old temple
legends.body: The Kazhakuttom Mahadeva Temple is believed to be 1000 years old.

tips.title: Check museum days.
tips.body: Most ticketed museums in Thiruvananthapuram are closed on Mondays.

tips.title: See the space museum.
tips.body: The old Pallithura church, founded by St. Francis Xavier, is now the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre's space museum.

story.title: An old temple
story.body: The Kazhakuttom Mahadeva Temple is believed to date back a thousand years.

story.title: The rebel's palace
story.body: Marthanda Varma defeated Ugran Pillai, destroyed his palace and put a pond in its place. He built a Krishna temple nearby, and both still survive.

story.title: Rockets next door
story.body: Pallithura villagers gave up their land for the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station.

story.title: Technopark
story.body: Technopark was planned in 1990 and dedicated to the nation on 18 November 1995.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Old temples, rockets and tech parks. Tell me which one surprised you most.
